Hi everyone, welcome back to the channel.
Today I'm going to talk about to-do lists, and before we start, make sure you subscribe.
So, a little background about me.
I have been writing to-do lists for about fifteen years now.
I've used paper notebooks, apps, sticky notes, whiteboards, you name it.
And for most of that time, the lists were mostly just there.
They sat on my desk and they sort of existed.
Why does your to-do list never actually get done?
It's not because you are lazy.
The real reason is that your list mixes three completely different kinds of work.
There are tasks that take five minutes, tasks that take five hours, and tasks that are really just wishes.
When you put all of them on one page, your brain sees a wall it can never finish.
So it picks the easiest item, crosses it off, and calls that progress.
Here is the simple rule that changed everything for me.
Every morning, pick one task that would make the whole day a success.
Just one.
Do it before you open your email, before you check your phone, before anything else.
Everything after that is a bonus.
I tried this for thirty days and I finished more real work than in the previous three months.
Now, let me tell you about my office setup.
I have a standing desk, which I use maybe half the time.
There is a plant in the corner that I keep forgetting to water.
The chair is fine, it's a normal chair.
Okay, back to the main point.
The biggest mistake people make is writing tasks as vague nouns.
If your list says taxes, you will never start, because taxes is not an action.
Write the very next physical step instead, like open the folder and find last year's form.
Your brain can start a step, but it cannot start a cloud.
Try rewriting just three items on your list tonight and watch what happens tomorrow.
That's about it for today.
Thank you so much for watching, and I'll see you in the next video.
